content:
Facts: Separated spouse and six children (from first marriage) challenged father's holographic will appointing cohabitant sole heir and recognizing natural son; claimed will apocryphal, vitiated by violence/fraud, ineffective lacking heir designation, alternatively seeking reduction for legitimate portion infringement; joined case addressed whether testator's mother's prior will (leaving apartment to testator as usufructuary, granddaughter as bare owner) revoked by subsequent will appointing testator universal heir.
Legal Framework: Articles 253-254, 537, 542, 556, 558, 587-591, 602, 606, 624, 682 Italian Civil Code (natural filiation recognition conflict with legitimate status; legitimate portions spouse-children; fictitious reunion; reduction; testamentary capacity/vices; holographic will formalities; fraud/violence; tacit revocation by incompatibility); Arts. 221 et seq. CPC (forgery complaint procedure).
Interpretive Issues: Procedural remedy for holographic will authenticity challenge (nullity action versus forgery complaint); admissibility of testamentary incapacity claim first raised as substantial mutatio libelli; fraud/violence requirements for will annulment; natural child recognition validity when conflicting with legitimate status; whether "sole cohabitant" designation constitutes valid heir appointment; tacit revocation by incompatibility (objective versus subjective) when subsequent will appoints universal heir after prior specific bequests; standing of pretermitted heirs to assert testator's inheritance rights in predecessor's succession; estate formation including predecessor's inheritance assets.
Principles Applied: Holographic will authenticity challenge requires forgery complaint per Arts. 221 et seq. CPC, not mere nullity action; will comparable to public deed following publication. Handwriting expert confirmation of autograph nature defeats apocrypha claim. Testamentary incapacity claim (Art. 591) inadmissible as substantial mutatio libelli when original writ alleged only fraud/violence vitiating consent (Arts. 1434, 1439); defect-of-consent versus incapacity constitute distinct grounds. Fraud/violence annulment requires fraudulent means (beyond flattery, requests, suggestions) considering testator's age/health/mental state, capable of misleading and directing will contrary to spontaneous direction; presumptive evidence must identify captative activity and decisive influence on decision-making. Hospital confrontation incidents post-dating will (occurred day before death versus will dated ten days prior) insufficient to prove prior fraud/violence. Estrangement conduct consistency with testator's exclusion intent negates fraud/violence inference; cohabitant's opposition to reconciliation absent deception/compulsion evidence inadequate. Natural child recognition per Arts. 254, 587(2) ineffective when contradicting legitimate status (Art. 253); continuing status conflict renders natural-filiation-based inheritance claims inadmissible pending legitimate-status disavowal finality. Testamentary expression interpretation per Art. 1362 principles seeks actual testator intention however expressed; "testamentary cohabitant" terminology interpreted as "testamentary heir" or involuntary crasis; conservation principle (Art. 1367) requires adoption of validating interpretation absent justification. Valid will appointing sole heir infringes reserved portions: separated spouse 1/4 (Art. 542); six children collectively 1/2 divided equally (Art. 537 as amended D.Lgs. 154/2013); available portion 1/4. Tacit revocation per Art. 682 encompasses: (a) objective/material incompatibility (logical/material/legal impossibility of simultaneous execution); (b) subjective/intentional incompatibility (inferring non-confirmation intent from clause nature/circumstances). Multiple complementary wills admissible absent incompatibility. Subsequent will appointing testator universal heir of "all remaining property" objectively incompatible with prior will leaving same testator usufruct and granddaughter bare ownership; "remaining property" means property remaining at death including previously bequeathed assets. Subjective incompatibility evidenced by granddaughter's complete omission in subsequent will. Prior will revoked by subsequent incompatible will; previously bequeathed property falls into testator's succession then into testator's estate. Pretermitted heirs lack standing to assert rights as testator's heirs before successful reduction action finality; standing arises during proceedings when reduction succeeds; action admissible if standing exists at decision time regardless when acquired. Fictitious reunion per Art. 556 forms estate totaling relictum (assets at death minus debts) plus donatum (donated assets at succession-opening value per Arts. 747, 750). Reserved portions calculated on formed estate; testamentary dispositions reduced proportionally within available portion limits to reinstate legitimate portions per Art. 558. Case remanded for supplemental expert assessment: rental value of disputed property; divisibility assessment per Art. 720; in-kind return feasibility per Art. 561; division plan preparation subject to party agreement per Arts. 788-789 considering conciliation possibilities. Judicial seizure maintained pending estate possession dispute resolution.
